messages:
anya: quick sync 1: prototyping a 'slimline' route-graph that ships deltas for hot keys instead of full policy pushes. idea is stripe-based diffs so routers see small updates. anyone see pitfalls?

leo: sounds promising for high qps tenants. main questions: 1) how do we guarantee ordering and idempotence of deltas? 2) what about joins when a router misses a delta?

rita: ordering: include monotonic seq + checksum per stripe. idempotence: ops should be replayable. missing-delta recovery: routers can request full snapshot on gap detection.

sam: we need to decide stripe granularity. per-tenant? per-route-prefix? Too fine-grained increases metadata overhead.

anya: thinking: shard by hash(route-id) into 64 stripes. most tenants will only touch a few stripes per minute.

leo: 64 seems reasonable but we should measure stripe hotspotting. extreme tenants might touch many stripes -> then deltas still big. fallback is to send compressed snapshot for that tenant.

rita: semantics: deltas must be causally consistent for policy evaluation. if a delta changes a route weight and another delta adds a constraint, routers must apply in order. seq + vector clock? vector clock across stripes is heavy.

sam: can we keep a single policy-revision number (monotonic) and tag each delta with that revision? routers apply only deltas for revision==current_rev+1; otherwise trigger resync. cheap and easier to reason about.

anya: yes: control plane compiles -> new revision N -> emits striped deltas with rev=N. router applies only if base_rev==N-1 and seqs contiguous; else resync.

leo: resync path must be cheap. recommend a small fast endpoint that returns compressed snapshot + optional debug mapping. routers can hot-swap snapshot and continue.

rita: durability: what if router applies delta then crashes before persisting rev? use atomic persist+apply. we need write-ahead on router disk or memory-mapped journal.

sam: we already have journal for route-cache; reuse it. ensure idempotent apply so replay is safe.

anya: security: signed deltas + per-revision nonce to prevent replay from older controllers.

leo: telemetry: we should include a small change-type in delta header (weight, constraint-add, constraint-remove, explain-id-update) so traces can annotate which change caused an outcome. keep header tiny.

rita: good. also include tombstones for removed routes so routers can GC deterministically. tombstone TTL tied to max-inflight-requests.

sam: GC TTL: we have request max-latency ~30s, but to be safe use 5 minutes. routers keep tombstone keys for 5m then fully delete.

anya: what about policy evaluation order changes across deltas? i.e., we change comparator that affects tie-breaker semantics; that may require coordinated rollout.

leo: for semantic changes that alter evaluation algorithm, prefer full snapshot + a rollout flag that indicates routers should switch algorithms only when snapshot_rev >= X. avoid partial delta-only upgrades.

rita: operational: we need fallback behavior when deltas fail verification or parsing: router should keep last good revision, emit alert, and optionally fallback to default-safe route. do not apply partial deltas.

sam: testing plan: fuzz apply-order, simulate missing-delta, crash-after-apply, and measure mean time to resync under load. add property test that final snapshot after replay matches compiled snapshot.

anya: implementation plan: I'll wire stripe encoder in control plane, emit signed delta stream + compressed snapshot endpoint. Sam will add router apply/journal code + resync. Rita will spec tombstone TTL and GC. Leo will own rollout gating for algorithm changes.

ops-bot: checklist created: https://tiny.redwood/checklists/route-deltas-slimline (auto) :white_check_mark:

anya: timeframe: prototype in 10 days, tests in 3 weeks. We'll post bench numbers and a short RFC with examples.

leo: one extra thought 1: expose a debug-mode that forces full snapshots for a router to aid local troubleshooting.

rita: +1. debug-mode should be opt-in and rate-limited.

sam: agreed. closing here, will open PRs for delta encoder and router journal.

anya: thanks all :rocket:
